newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa may sell off over 30 pct of SAA.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa may sell off over 30 pct of SAA.

text.p: South Africa's Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Tuesday the government aimed to accelerate the partial privatisation of South African Airways and could sell more than an originally foreseen 25-30 percent stake.

"Government policy is to speed up the restructuring of SAA," Sigcau told reporters at a briefing in Cape Town, explaining this would enhance the flag carrier's position in an increasingly competitive market.
"It does have some problems and the competition is becoming thicker by the day. We want to fast track the restructuring."

Sigcau said the government had been been thinking of selling a 25-30 stake to a strategic equity partner in SAA but that this was being reconsidered following a rethink of privatisation plans for Sun Air.
Sigcau announced on Monday that the government had decided to offer 49 percent of state-run Sun Air to foreign buyers, instead of the 25 percent initially planned.

A "very important" workshop on SAA would be held on February 25-26 to thrash out plans further, Sigcau added. The talks would involve government representatives, labour officials, executives from the Transnet parastatal of which SAA is a part and parliamentarians.
Potential foreign investors would not participate in the workshop.

Sigcau gave no indication of likely foreign partners for SAA, but industry attention has focused on Germany's Lufthansa which already has a cooperation deal with the airline covering code-sharing, frequent flyer programmes and cargo operations.
